### Greene County Bancorp, Inc. Reports Record High Net Income of $12.5 Million for the Quarter Ended September 30, 2026, an Increase of 41% when Compared to the Quarter Ended September 30, 2025


October 22, 2026


CATSKILL, N.Y., Oct. 22, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Greene County Bancorp, Inc. (the “Company”) (NASDAQ: GCBC), the holding company for Bank of Greene (formerly the Bank of Greene County) and its subsidiary Greene County Commercial Bank, today reported net income for the three months ended September 30, 2026, which is the first quarter of the Company’s fiscal year ending June 30, 2027. Net income for the three months ended September 30, 2026 was $12.5 million, or $0.73 per basic and diluted share, as compared to $8.9 million, or $0.52 per basic and diluted share, for the three months ended September 30, 2025. Net income increased $3.6 million, or 40.9%, when comparing the three months ended September 30, 2026 and 2025.


Highlights:


- Net Income: $12.5 million for the three months ended September 30, 2026, a new record high
- Total Assets: $3.2 billion at September 30, 2026, a new record high
- Net Loans: $1.8 billion at September 30, 2026, a new record high
- Total Deposits: $2.8 billion at September 30, 2026, a new record high
- Return on Average Assets: 1.61% for the three months ended September 30, 2026
- Return on Average Equity: 17.73% for the three months ended September 30, 2026


“This quarter marked an important milestone as we introduced the Bank of Greene name and delivered record quarterly earnings,” said Donald Gibson, President & CEO. “Our new name reflects the broader region we serve and the relationships we continue to build across the Hudson Valley and Capital Region. Our commitment remains rooted in responsive personal service and local decision making. We are proud of our employees and remain focused on growing responsibly, supporting our customers, and delivering long-term shareholder value.”


Effective September 14, 2026, the Company’s primary banking subsidiary changed its legal name from the Bank of Greene County to Bank of Greene. The name change has no impact on the Bank’s operations and has no impact on the Company’s consolidated financial statements.


At the Company’s Annual Meeting on November 7, 2026, shareholders will consider a related proposal to amend the Company’s charter to change its legal name from Greene County Bancorp, Inc. to Greene Bancorp, Inc. If approved, the name change is expected to become effective following certification of the shareholder vote on November 9, 2026. The Company’s Nasdaq trading symbol “GCBC” and CUSIP number are not expected to change.


Total consolidated assets for the Company were $3.2 billion at September 30, 2026, primarily consisting of $1.8 billion of net loans and $1.2 billion of total securities available-for-sale and held-to-maturity. Consolidated deposits totaled $2.8 billion at September 30, 2026, consisting of retail, business, municipal and private banking relationships.


Pre-provision net income was $12.1 million for the three months ended September 30, 2026 as compared to $10.1 million for the three months ended September 30, 2025, an increase of $1.9 million, or 19.2%. Pre-provision net income measures the Company’s net income not including the provision for credit losses. Management believes that this non-GAAP measure assists investors in comprehending the impact of the provision for credit losses on the Company’s reported results, offering an alternative view of the Company’s performance and the Company’s ability to generate income in excess of its provision for credit losses.


The Company continues to manage its balance sheet with a focus on higher-yielding loans and securities, and disciplined deposit pricing. Deposit rates are actively managed in response to market interest rates and competitive conditions. These efforts contributed to a higher net interest margin for the three months ended September 30, 2026, compared with the same period in 2025.


Uncertainty surrounding inflation, the direction of interest rates, and geopolitical developments continues to influence the economic outlook. The Company remains focused on prudent risk management, maintaining financial strength and pursuing profitable growth, while delivering long-term shareholder value and serving the financial needs of its communities.


Selected highlights for the three months ended September 30, 2026, are as follows:


Net Interest Income and Margin


- **Net interest income** increased $4.4 million to $21.9 million for the three months ended September 30, 2026, from $17.5 million for the three months ended September 30, 2025. The increase in net interest income was primarily due to an increase in the average balance of interest-earning assets, which increased $159.3 million when comparing the three months ended September 30, 2026 and 2025, an increase in the average yield on interest-earning assets, which increased 16 basis points when comparing the three months ended September 30, 2026 and 2025, and a decrease in the average rate paid on interest-bearing liabilities, which decreased 30 basis points when comparing the three months ended September 30, 2026 and 2025. The increase in net interest income was offset by an increase in the average balance of interest-bearing liabilities, which increased $101.8 million when comparing the three months ended September 30, 2026 and 2025.


Average loan balances increased $113.6 million and the yield on such loans increased 12 basis points when comparing the three months ended September 30, 2026 and 2025. The average balance of securities increased $58.4 million and the yield on such securities increased 24 basis points when comparing the three months ended September 30, 2026 and 2025. The average interest-bearing bank balances and federal funds decreased $14.6 million and the yield on interest-bearing bank balances and federal funds decreased 125 basis points when comparing the three months ended September 30, 2026 and 2025.


The cost of NOW deposits decreased 39 basis points, the cost of certificates of deposits decreased 25 basis points, and the cost of savings and money market deposits decreased 4 basis points when comparing the three months ended September 30, 2026 and 2025. The growth in the average interest-bearing liabilities was primarily due to an increase in certificates of deposits of $51.8 million, an increase in average NOW deposits of $32.7 million, and an increase in average savings and money market deposits of $489,000 when comparing the three months ended September 30, 2026 and 2025. When comparing the three months ended September 30, 2026 and 2025, yields on interest-earning assets increased while the costs of interest-bearing deposits declined, reflecting continued asset repricing and the Company’s strategic reduction in deposit rates.


- **Net interest rate spread** increased 46 basis points to 2.71% for the three months ended September 30, 2026 as compared to 2.25% for the three months ended September 30, 2025.
**Net interest margin** increased 45 basis points to 2.93% for the three months ended September 30, 2026 as compared to 2.48% for the three months ended September 30, 2025. The improvement reflected higher yields on loans and securities, combined with lower deposit costs, including reduced rates paid on NOW accounts and certificates of deposit. These benefits more than offset the decline in yields on interest-bearing bank balances and federal funds, supporting margin expansion alongside balance sheet growth.


- **Net interest income on a taxable-equivalent basis** includes the additional amount of interest income that would have been earned if the Company’s investment in tax-exempt securities and loans had been subject to federal and New York State income taxes yielding the same after-tax income. Tax-equivalent net interest margin increased 46 basis points to 3.24% for the three months ended September 30, 2026, from 2.78% for the three months ended September 30, 2025.


Credit Quality and Provision for Credit Losses


- **Provision for credit losses** amounted to a benefit of $432,000 for the three months ended September 30, 2026 as compared to a charge of $1.3 million for the three months ended September 30, 2025. The benefit for the three months ended September 30, 2026, was primarily attributable to the release of the allowance for credit losses associated with an individually evaluated loan that was repaid in full during the quarter, as well as improvements in the economic forecasts used in the Current Expected Credit Loss (“CECL”) model. The allowance for credit losses on loans to total loans receivable was 1.21% at September 30, 2026 as compared to 1.25% at June 30, 2026.


- **Commercial and commercial real estate loans classified** as substandard and special mention totaled $30.8 million at September 30, 2026, and $40.0 million at June 30, 2026, a decrease of $9.2 million. The decrease in the commercial and commercial real estate loans classified during the period ended September 30, 2026 was primarily due to upgrades of commercial real estate and commercial loans that were considered to be performing and paying in accordance with the terms of their loan agreements, and commercial real estate and commercial loans that were paid off during the period. Of the loans classified as substandard or special mention, $29.9 million were performing at September 30, 2026. There were no loans classified as doubtful or loss at September 30, 2026 or June 30, 2026.


- **Net charge-offs on loans** amounted to $48,000 and $60,000 for the three months ended September 30, 2026 and 2025, respectively, a decrease of $12,000. There were no material charge-offs in any loan segment during the three months ended September 30, 2026.


- **Nonperforming loans** amounted to $3.2 million at September 30, 2026 and $3.9 million at June 30, 2026. The activity in nonperforming loans during the period included $1.2 million in loan repayments, $163,000 in loans returning to performing status, $91,000 in charge-offs or transfers to foreclosure, and $720,000 of loans placed into nonperforming status. At September 30, 2026, nonperforming assets were 0.10% of total assets as compared to 0.12% at June 30, 2026. At September 30, 2026, nonperforming loans were 0.18% of net loans as compared to 0.23% at June 30, 2026.


Noninterest Income and Noninterest Expense


- **Noninterest income** decreased $1.1 million, or 27.0%, to $2.9 million for the three months ended September 30, 2026 as compared to $4.0 million for the three months ended September 30, 2025. The decrease during the three months ended September 30, 2026 was primarily due to a $1.2 million loss on sales of securities available-for-sale and a decrease of $289,000 in income earned on customer interest rate swaps. This was partially offset by a $140,000 increase in investment services income.


- **Noninterest expense** increased $740,000, or 7.4%, to $10.8 million for the three months ended September 30, 2026 as compared to $10.1 million for the three months ended September 30, 2025. The increase during the three months ended September 30, 2026 was primarily due to an increase of $582,000 in salaries and employee benefits and an increase of $367,000 in the allowance for credit losses unfunded commitment expense, due to an increase in the Company’s contractual obligation to extend credit.


Income Taxes


- **Provision for income taxes** reflects the expected tax associated with the pre-tax income generated for the given period and certain regulatory requirements. The effective tax rate was 13.4% for the three months ended September 30, 2026 and 12.9% for the three months ended September 30, 2025. The statutory tax rate is impacted by the benefits derived from tax-exempt bond and loan income, the Company’s real estate investment trust subsidiary income, income received on the bank owned life insurance and tax credits to arrive at the effective tax rate. The increase during the three months ended September 30, 2026 was primarily due to higher mix of pre-tax income and reflects a lower mix of tax-exempt income from municipal bonds, tax advantage loans, and bank owned life insurance in proportion to pre-tax income.


Balance Sheet Summary


- **Total assets** of the Company were $3.2 billion at September 30, 2026 and June 30, 2026.


- **Total cash and cash equivalents** for the Company were $135.0 million at September 30, 2026 and $144.9 million at June 30, 2026. The Company has continued to maintain strong capital and liquidity positions as of September 30, 2026.


- **Securities available-for-sale and held-to-maturity** increased $48.6 million, or 4.1%, to $1.23 billion at September 30, 2026 as compared to $1.18 billion at June 30, 2026. Securities purchased totaled $148.1 million during the three months ended September 30, 2026, primarily consisting of $125.2 million of state and political subdivision securities, $13.9 million of mortgage-backed securities, and $9.0 million of collateralized mortgage obligations. Principal pay-downs and maturities during the three months ended September 30, 2026, amounted to $87.0 million, primarily consisting of $66.8 million of state and political subdivision securities, $13.0 million of mortgage-backed securities, $3.0 million in U.S. Treasuries, $3.0 million in corporate debt securities, and $1.2 million of collateralized mortgage obligations.


- **Net loans receivable** increased $23.1 million, or 1.3%, to $1.8 billion at September 30, 2026 as compared to $1.7 billion at June 30, 2026. Loan growth experienced during the three months ended September 30, 2026, consisted primarily of $18.3 million in commercial real estate loans, $3.7 million in commercial loans, and $2.5 million in home equity loans. The allowance for credit losses on loans decreased $417,000, or 1.9%, to $21.4 million at September 30, 2026 as compared to $21.9 million at June 30, 2026. The decrease in the allowance for credit losses was primarily attributable to the release of the allowance for credit losses associated with an individually evaluated loan that was repaid in full during the quarter, as well as improvements in the economic forecasts used in the CECL model.


- **Deposits** totaled $2.8 billion at September 30, 2026 as compared to $2.7 billion at June 30, 2026, an increase of $134.4 million, or 5.0%. The Company had $41.6 million and $52.4 million of brokered deposits at September 30, 2026 and June 30, 2026, respectively. NOW deposits increased $111.3 million, or 5.6%, certificates of deposits increased $19.1 million, or 7.7%, and noninterest bearing deposits increased $13.9 million, or 9.9%, when comparing September 30, 2026 and June 30, 2026. Savings deposits decreased $5.5 million, or 2.3%, and money market deposits decreased $4.4 million, or 4.4%, when comparing September 30, 2026 and June 30, 2026.


- **Borrowings** amounted to $66.2 million at September 30, 2026 as compared to $155.1 million at June 30, 2026, a decrease of $88.9 million. At September 30, 2026, borrowings included $40.0 million of overnight borrowings with the Federal Home Loan Bank of New York (“FHLB”), $20.0 million of Fixed-to-Floating Rate Subordinated Notes and $6.2 million of long-term borrowings with the FHLB.


As previously announced, on September 15, 2026, the Company redeemed $10.0 million in aggregate principal amount of the $30.0 million 3.00% Fixed-to-Floating Rate Subordinated Notes, due September 15, 2031. Following the redemption, $20.0 million in aggregate principal amount of the Notes remains outstanding. The redemption was funded by cash on hand.


- **Shareholders’ equity** increased to $286.0 million at September 30, 2026 as compared to $277.8 million at June 30, 2026, resulting primarily from net income of $12.5 million, partially offset by an increase in accumulated other comprehensive loss of $3.5 million and dividends declared and paid of $859,000. Under the Company’s current stock repurchase program, there were no repurchases during the three months ended September 30, 2026. As of the three months ended September 30, 2026, 398,657 shares remain in the stock repurchase program.


**Corporate Overview**


Greene County Bancorp, Inc. is the holding company for Bank of Greene, and its subsidiary Greene County Commercial Bank. The Company is the leading provider of community-based banking services throughout the Hudson Valley and Capital Region of New York State. Its customers include individuals, businesses, municipalities and other institutions. Greene County Bancorp, Inc. (GCBC) is publicly traded on the Nasdaq Capital Market and is dedicated to promoting economic development and a high quality of life in the communities it serves. For more information on Greene County Bancorp, Inc., visit[www.bankofgreene.com](https://www.globenewswire.com/Tracker?data=ibCxP1L8txFmQus8buG3s8ZtVOLZO0M05xvkkcRcHN2GhZuNE2s6jYE4NBnZluM9zgpMqHklnEJTaxQ1oVq1755lBE3H-bnoaUrdMkLPl0I=) .
